newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Indian Ocean lines in vessel sharing agreement.
newsitem.headline: Indian Ocean lines in vessel sharing agreement.

text.p: Three shipping lines have entered into a vessel sharing agreement covering their services between South Africa, east Africa, the Indian sub-continent and Arabian Gulf, said.
The three lines are Durban-based Unicorn-CMBT lines, Mauritius' Laurel Navigation and P&O Containers of London.

The agreement, which will also integrate sailing schedules, will for the first time offer importers and exporters in the region a high frequency service, with a sailing every eight days, Agent Ellerman & Bucknall said in a statement.
The combination of the existing fleet of seven vessels into a single, integrated schedule will also provide the widest port coverage with fast transit times between the main ports.

All vessels will call at Durban, Dar es Salaam, Mombasa, Karachi, Jebel Ali and Mumbai before returning to Durban via East Africa. In addition, vessels will call at Nacala, Beira and Colombo on an alternate basis.
